-- 145_retire_admissions_and_connections_in_place.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-050; OD-29, resolved under delegation: a connection and a search-to-source admission edge are
-- data rows under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-16, "RETIRE IN PLACE, NEVER HARD-DELETE"; a genuine deletion of either
-- is an exception only the owner rules on). No data rows.
--
-- `search_admissions` and `connections` each gain the retirement shape `specifications` and `extraction_lens_links`
-- already use: `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retirement_reason`, nullable, set together or not at all. The
-- CHECK sits on the last of the three, because SQLite adds a column by ALTER and a column constraint may name its
-- siblings. `connection_targets` gains nothing: a target of a retired connection is retired through its pointer.
--
-- THE RULING'S EXECUTION CONDITION: "No row is retired in place until every reader that could surface it filters on
-- status." The two views that read `search_admissions` filter below; every other reader of either table is a script and
-- is fixed in the same pull request (db.py, research_batch_dod.py, test_db_integrity.py, graph/extract_db.py).
--  * v_source_admission, from its current text in sqlite_master (migration 070 set it), gains `AND sa.retired_at IS NULL`:
--    a withdrawn attribution is not "the search that admitted this source".
--  * v_coverage_parameter_via_admission, from its current text (migration 140 set it), gains the same predicate in the
--    `reached` CTE: a search does not reach a parameter through an admission it has withdrawn. No view reads
--    `connections` or `connection_targets`.
-- The retired edge stays a row: it is the record that the claim was made, when, by whom and why it was withdrawn, and it
-- is never un-retired in place (db.py link-admission refuses it and names log-search).
-- WRITERS: db.py unlink-admission and delete-connection (each now sets the three columns instead of deleting).
-- READERS: the two views above, db.py get_connections, db.py's parameter reach, research_batch_dod R17,
-- test_db_integrity S01 and the graph extractor.

ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE search_admissions ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE connections ADD COLUMN retirement_reason TEXT
  CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL));

DROP VIEW v_source_admission;
CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.evidence_type,
    es.verification_status,
    es.verification_disposition,
    se.exec_id,
    se.slug                     AS admitted_under_slug,
    se.query_text,
    se.engine,
    se.language,
    se.jurisdiction             AS search_jurisdiction,
    se.depth_method,
    se.mining_direction,
    se.target_tier,
    se.backfill                 AS search_was_backfilled,
    se.created_by_session                  AS admitting_session,
    se.created_at              AS admitted_at,
    -- The research-stage prior, reached by pointer rather than copied onto the
    -- evidence row. This is what makes CHECK 7 answerable.
    se.prior_expectation
FROM evidence_sources es
JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.ref_id  = es.ref_id AND sa.retired_at IS NULL
JOIN search_executions se ON se.exec_id = sa.exec_id;

DROP VIEW v_coverage_parameter_via_admission;
CREATE VIEW v_coverage_parameter_via_admission AS
WITH searched AS (
  SELECT se.exec_id, se.parameter_id, UPPER(se.language) AS language,
         COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction) AS jurisdiction
    FROM search_executions se
    LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction
   WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NULL),
reached AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.exec_id, s.language, s.jurisdiction, x.parameter_id, sa.ref_id
    FROM searched s
    JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.exec_id = s.exec_id AND sa.retired_at IS NULL
    JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = sa.ref_id AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
    JOIN source_value_extractions x ON x.ref_id = sa.ref_id
   WHERE x.claim_type <> 'absent' AND COALESCE(x.extraction_method, '') <> 'skim')
SELECT p.parameter_id, v.language, v.jurisdiction, v.role,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM searched s WHERE s.language = v.language AND s.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction)
           AS searches_ran_in_pair,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM searched s WHERE s.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND s.language = v.language AND s.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_naming_parameter,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.exec_id) FROM reached r WHERE r.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND r.language = v.language AND r.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_reaching_parameter,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.ref_id) FROM reached r WHERE r.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND r.language = v.language AND r.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS sources_admitted,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_jurisdictions j WHERE j.jurisdiction_code = v.jurisdiction) AS jurisdiction_registered
  FROM base_parameters p CROSS JOIN v_research_scope v
 WHERE p.status = 'active';

PRAGMA user_version = 145;
-- 146_term_forms_occurrence.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- a concept is its id; its names are forms, one row per occurrence; `canonical_en` is our label.
-- Tooling (IMP-21, workplan T-028; design workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-028-design.md, revised
-- 2026-11-13; delegated resolution of OD-03; OD-38 answered by the owner 2026-11-12, "First recorded, until a named
-- judge picks; the pick is recorded with its reason"). No research rows.
--
-- AFTER_DATA: 20261106053823
-- (Why the marker: `migrate_db.py --rebuild` runs schema migrations before the data migrations that follow the last
-- marker, and data migrations may insert term_aliases rows; without it a data migration landed after 130 would replay
-- after this reshape and the rebuild would diverge. Value: the newest data migration at the time of writing, derived by
-- `ls scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | sed -E 's/.*data_([0-9]{14})_.*/\1/' | sort | tail -1`.)
--
-- WHAT CHANGES (design sections 3, 7 and 10):
--  1. term_aliases is rebuilt to ONE ROW PER OCCURRENCE: a surrogate key `form_id` (assigned here, once, from each row's
--     rowid; the rebuild reproduces it and nothing stored points by rowid), a unique occurrence index in place of the
--     primary key (term_id, alias, language), and a nullable `usage_type` (NULL = not yet typed, the truth for every
--     existing row; typed by judgment when the row is next touched, never guessed here). The column definitions T-026
--     added are copied from sqlite_master, so `attestation` keeps its DEFAULT 'unrecorded'. Legacy alias_type values
--     are not rewritten.
--  2. T-026's junction search_execution_forms is remapped BY KEY to form_id before the old table is dropped: at the
--     occurrence grain the old key is no longer unique, and a foreign key on it would answer `foreign key mismatch`.
--     Until now one row per key, so the join is exact and the junction's row count does not change.
--  3. term_label_picks: the one home of the judge, the reason and the former label of a label set by judgment (OD-38).
--     The route is derived from which pointer is set; the new label is terms.canonical_en, never copied here.
--  4. v_term_names: the name shown (E1) and whether our label is also an attested form, derived; no label-kind column
--     and no display pointer is stored.
-- No VACUUM: it may renumber the implicit rowids of every table without an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY.

CREATE TABLE _146_term_aliases (
    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(alias_type IN (
                            'SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER',
                            'BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN'
                        )),
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded'
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),
    source_url          TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'
         OR source_url GLOB 'https://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')
        AND source_url NOT GLOB '*[' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')),
    source_page         TEXT
    CHECK (source_page IS NULL OR TRIM(source_page, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    source_line         INTEGER
    CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR (typeof(source_line) = 'integer' AND source_line > 0)),
    source_clause       TEXT
    CHECK (
        (source_clause IS NULL OR TRIM(source_clause, char(32,9,10,13)) <> '') AND
        -- an attested occurrence says where
        (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
         OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL)))
        -- a seed or an unrecorded form says nowhere
        AND (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL
             AND source_clause IS NULL))
    ),
    -- the sixth statement of 2026-11-06's usage types, in this column's own CHECK (read by dbcore.check_values)
    usage_type          TEXT
    CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN
        ('code_term','colloquial','regional_variant','outdated_or_disfavoured','product_name'))
);

INSERT INTO _146_term_aliases (form_id, term_id, alias, language, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes, created_at,
                               created_by_session, updated_at, updated_by_session, observation_id, attestation,
                               source_url, source_page, source_line, source_clause, usage_type)
SELECT rowid, term_id, alias, language, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes, created_at,
       created_by_session, updated_at, updated_by_session, observation_id, attestation,
       source_url, source_page, source_line, source_clause, NULL

CREATE TABLE terms (
    term_id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    canonical_en        TEXT NOT NULL,
    definition          TEXT,
    domain              TEXT,
    scope_note          TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL
, catalogue TEXT
    CHECK (catalogue IN ('references/standards-registry.md', 'references/tier456-verified-sources.json', 'references/co1-verified-sources.json', 'references/co2-verified-sources.json', '_archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db')), catalogue_entry_ref TEXT, catalogue_approval_ref TEXT
    CHECK ((catalogue IS NULL AND catalogue_entry_ref IS NULL AND catalogue_approval_ref IS NULL)
        OR (catalogue IS NOT NULL
            AND catalogue_entry_ref IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(catalogue_entry_ref)) > 0
            AND catalogue_approval_ref IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(catalogue_approval_ref)) > 0)))

CREATE TABLE term_label_picks (
    pick_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    former_label        TEXT,                                               -- NULL only for a mint by add-term --first-form
    form_id             INTEGER REFERENCES term_aliases(form_id),          -- rename-term --from-form, or a mint's first form
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id), -- rename-term --from-observation
    ruling_quote        TEXT,                                               -- rename-term --ruling-quote
    judge               TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- who picked
    reason              TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- why (add-term --first-form: its --rationale)
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((form_id IS NOT NULL) + (observation_id IS NOT NULL) + (ruling_quote IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (former_label IS NOT NULL OR form_id IS NOT NULL)
)

CREATE TABLE translations (
    translation_id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    source_table                 TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(source_table)) > 0),
    source_column                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(source_column)) > 0),
    source_row_key               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(source_row_key)) > 0),
    source_sha256                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(source_sha256) = 64),
    target_language              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(target_language)) > 0),
    translated_text              TEXT CHECK (translated_text IS NULL OR length(trim(translated_text)) > 0),
    status                       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requested'
                                 CHECK (status IN ('requested', 'translated', 'reviewed', 'rejected')),
    translator_kind              TEXT CHECK (translator_kind IS NULL OR translator_kind IN ('model', 'tool', 'person')),
    translator_name              TEXT CHECK (translator_name IS NULL OR length(trim(translator_name)) > 0),
    requested_at_stage           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(requested_at_stage)) > 0),
    due_stage                    TEXT CHECK (due_stage IS NULL OR length(trim(due_stage)) > 0),
    reviewed_by_kind             TEXT CHECK (reviewed_by_kind IS NULL OR reviewed_by_kind IN ('model', 'tool', 'person')),
    reviewed_by_name             TEXT CHECK (reviewed_by_name IS NULL OR length(trim(reviewed_by_name)) > 0),
    reviewed_at                  TEXT,
    review_reason                TEXT CHECK (review_reason IS NULL OR length(trim(review_reason)) > 0),
    superseded_by_translation_id INTEGER REFERENCES translations(translation_id),
    created_at                   TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session           TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at                   TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session           TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- text exists exactly once the request has been answered
    CHECK ((status = 'requested') = (translated_text IS NULL)),
    -- who translated it: none while requested, both once past it
    CHECK ((status = 'requested' AND translator_kind IS NULL AND translator_name IS NULL)
        OR (status <> 'requested' AND translator_kind IS NOT NULL AND translator_name IS NOT NULL)),
    -- who reviewed it: all three exactly when reviewed or rejected, and never the translator (OD-30)
    CHECK ((status IN ('reviewed', 'rejected')
            AND reviewed_by_kind IS NOT NULL AND reviewed_by_name IS NOT NULL AND reviewed_at IS NOT NULL)
        OR (status NOT IN ('reviewed', 'rejected')
            AND reviewed_by_kind IS NULL AND reviewed_by_name IS NULL AND reviewed_at IS NULL)),
    CHECK (reviewed_by_name IS NULL OR reviewed_by_name <> translator_name),
    -- a rejection says why; a row that was not reviewed holds no reason
    CHECK (status <> 'rejected' OR review_reason IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (status IN ('reviewed', 'rejected') OR review_reason IS NULL),
    CHECK (superseded_by_translation_id IS NULL OR superseded_by_translation_id <> translation_id)
)

CREATE TABLE term_adjudications (
    adjudication_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    observation_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    -- OUTCOMES, documented HERE and not inside the CHECK. dbcore.check_values() reads
    -- this constraint's own value list to build the CLI's refusal, and an inline
    -- comment between the quoted values defeats its parser -- measured 2026-09-03,
    -- when a first cut of this migration carried the descriptions inside the IN(...)
    -- and every legitimate outcome was refused with a mangled vocabulary. The whole
    -- reason vocabularies come from the schema rather than a list in the code
    -- (CLAUDE.md §4) is defeated by punctuation the parser cannot see past.
    --
    --   NAMES-EXISTING  names a term we already hold
    --   NAMES-NEW       names a concept new to the vocabulary
    --   NOT-OURS        a real phrase, but not one of our concepts
    --   DEFERRED        cannot be settled on this source alone
    outcome             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
                            ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')),
    term_id             TEXT REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    -- NOT NULL: an adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested, and the
    -- whole point of splitting observation from judgment is that the judgement is
    -- inspectable.
    rationale           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- The outcome and the pointer must agree. An outcome that names a term must name
    -- one; an outcome that declines must not.
    CHECK (
        (outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND term_id IS NOT NULL)
     OR (outcome IN ('NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')        AND term_id IS NULL)
    )
)

CREATE TABLE "observed_terms" (
    observation_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    -- POINTER, not a copy. The source's bibliography stays in evidence_sources.
    ref_id              TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
    -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts.
    surface_form        TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The language the phrase APPEARS IN, which need not be the source's language.
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    -- R3's locator discipline: where in the source it appears. Part of the sighting's
    -- key since migration 102 (ux_observed_terms_sighting below).
    locator             TEXT,
    -- Enough surrounding text that judgment can adjudicate without re-retrieving.
    context_quote       TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT
)

CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
WITH attested AS (
    SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
      FROM term_aliases
     WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
       AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')),
en_instrument AS (
    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
pick AS (
    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
      FROM terms t)
SELECT p.term_id,
       p.canonical_en AS label,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_attested_form,

import zipfile
import sqlite3
import sys
import argparse
from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

# MOVED TO scripts/dbcore.py 2026-08-25. This module now IMPORTS the connection,
# path, audit-stamp and reference-id mechanics it used to own privately -- it was the
# only correct implementation in the repository and it had zero importers, so 55 other
# files re-implemented it 104 times and inherited none of its lessons.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
# The REPO ROOT too, so `schemas.*` resolves. add-source derives the ratified tier from
# schemas/tier_derivation.py rather than re-stating the ladder here — a second copy of a
# ratified rule is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and this CLI's whole value is that it
# refuses from the one authority rather than from a list of its own.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
import dbcore                                                      # noqa: E402
# The ONE dbcore name imported bare rather than reached through the module: it is raised,
# not called, and a module path in front of it at 114 sites crowds the line whose whole job
# is to carry a sentence. See dbcore.Refusal for why these are a subclass rather than plain
# ValueError -- in short, so that a defect keeps the traceback a refusal does not need.
from dbcore import Refusal                                         # noqa: E402


_ARGS = None   # main()'s parsed namespace: argparse takes abbreviations of any length, so the catch sites read the session from it


def _record(sentence):
    """Keep what this process said no to (T-088): a Refusal, a JSON error, a usage error, or a crash."""
    dbcore.record_refusal("scripts/db.py", sys.argv[1:], sentence, session=getattr(_ARGS, "session", None))


def _json_refusal(sentence):
    """The verbs that answer in JSON refuse as `{"error": ...}` and exit 2: the same refusal as a `Refusal`, kept (T-088)."""
    _record(sentence)
    print(json.dumps({"error": sentence}))
    sys.exit(2)


def _retrieval_log():
    """`scripts/research/retrieval_log`, imported on first use.

    It lives beside the bytes and outside the write path on purpose (its own docstring says
    why), and most verbs never need it, so it is not imported at module load.
    """
    research = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "research")
    if research not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, research)
    import retrieval_log                                              # noqa: E402
    return retrieval_log


def _ladder_evidence_types():
    """The evidence-type vocabulary, from the ratified ladder (CLAUDE.md rule 8).

    `schemas/tier_derivation.TIER_MAP`'s keys are the authority `add-source` already
    validates against. Used for argparse `choices=` where the column being written
    declares no CHECK of its own, so `dbcore.schema_choices()` has nothing to read.

    Returns None rather than raising if schemas is not importable: a parser that cannot
    be built is worse than one without a choices constraint, and the writer refuses the
    same values at run time either way.
    """
    try:
        from schemas.tier_derivation import TIER_MAP                 # noqa: E402
        return sorted({et for et, _ in TIER_MAP})
    except Exception:
        return None

    # No choices=: the amendable set is every live column less the named exclusions (GAP-013), so
    # a list here would be the second home it removed; the writer's refusal names the live set.
    p_amx.add_argument("--field", required=True,
                       help="A column of source_value_extractions that is not excluded (the refusal "
                            "lists them). claimed_value, claimed_unit and setting take a reformat "
                            "only (same numbers; a unit already in the cell, or its notation family's spelling of it; an empty setting; OR-3). "
                            "A different figure is a SECOND ROW and a contest (D-0168).")
    p_amx.add_argument("--value", required=True)
    p_amx.add_argument("--reason", required=True,
                       help="Why. Appended to notes, never overwriting it.")
    p_amx.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_amx.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    # add-lens-link / retire-lens-link -- a figure's lens is a set of links (OR-1c, migration 131).
    p_all = sub.add_parser("add-lens-link",
                           help="State an existing figure in one more lens code, with the words that "
                                "warrant it (replaces a carried link for the same code in one act)")
    p_all.add_argument("--extraction-id", dest="extraction_id", type=int, required=True)
    p_all.add_argument("--identity", help="base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code")
    p_all.add_argument("--icf", help="base_icf.icf_code — a real ICF b/d code")
    p_all.add_argument("--needs", help="access_needs.need_code")
    p_all.add_argument("--basis", required=True, choices=_lens_basis_choices(),
                       help="Live vocabulary, read from extraction_lens_links.basis's own CHECK ('carried' is "
                            "written only by migration 131)")
    p_all.add_argument("--basis-text", dest="basis_text", required=True,
                       help="The exact words that warrant the link: found in the figure's own words, in a "
                            "file saved for its source, or (study_participants) in a graded study_population")
    p_all.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_all.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    p_rll = sub.add_parser("retire-lens-link",
                           help="Retire one lens link in place (never the figure's last live one)")
    p_rll.add_argument("--link-id", dest="link_id", type=int, required=True)
    p_rll.add_argument("--reason", required=True)
    p_rll.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_rll.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    # derive-extraction -- a figure_role='derived' row, computed base+delta, plus
    # the two derived_from edges v_derived_figure_check re-verifies it against.
    p_dx = sub.add_parser("derive-extraction",
                          help="Write a computed (base+delta) extraction and the "
                               "derived_from edges that prove it")
    p_dx.add_argument("--ref-id", default=None,
                      help="OPTIONAL check only: the derived row is filed under its inputs' source (the base's), "
                           "and a different value is refused")
    p_dx.add_argument("--parameter-id", dest="parameter_id", type=int, required=True)
    _add_lens_flags(p_dx)
    p_dx.add_argument("--base", type=int, required=True,
                      help="extraction_id of the base figure")
    p_dx.add_argument("--delta", type=int, required=True,
                      help="extraction_id of the delta figure")
    p_dx.add_argument("--claimed-value", dest="claimed_value",
                      help="Omit to compute base + delta; a value given is CHECKED against it and refused if it differs. "
                           "The comparator, the unit, the quote, the locator and the source are the inputs' and are "
                           "never asked for")
    p_dx.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p_dx.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    p_adj = sub.add_parser("adjudicate-term",
                           help="Decide whether an observed phrase names our concept "
                                "(judgment stage, D-0173)")
                               args.reason, session=args.session,
                               dry_run=args.dry_run))

    elif args.command == "add-lens-link":
        _emit(add_lens_link(args.extraction_id, args.session, identity=args.identity, icf=args.icf,
                            needs=args.needs, basis=args.basis,
                            basis_text=args.basis_text, dry_run=args.dry_run))

    elif args.command == "retire-lens-link":
        _emit(retire_lens_link(args.link_id, args.reason, args.session, dry_run=args.dry_run))

    elif args.command == "derive-extraction":
        _emit(derive_extraction(
            ref_id=args.ref_id, parameter_id=args.parameter_id,
            identity=args.identity, icf=args.icf, needs=args.needs,
            lens_basis=args.lens_basis,
            lens_basis_text=args.lens_basis_text, base=args.base, delta=args.delta,
            claimed_value=args.claimed_value, session=args.session, dry_run=args.dry_run))

    elif args.command == "adjudicate-term":
        _emit(adjudicate_term(args.observation_id, args.outcome, args.rationale,

                input_role=edge.get("input_role"), notes=edge.get("notes"),

                session=session, context="add-extraction"))

def add_lens_link(extraction_id: int, session: str, *, identity: str = None, icf: str = None,
                  needs: str = None, basis: str = None, basis_text: str = None,
                  dry_run: bool = False):
    """State an existing figure in ONE more lens code (OR-1c), with the words that warrant it.

    Refuses: a figure that does not exist; none or more than one code; a code the registry lacks or a
    retired identity (`_require_lens_code`); a missing basis, a blank or unfound warrant
    (`_require_lens_warrant`); a live link already holding the code, EXCEPT a `carried` one, which is
    retired in this same transaction ("superseded by judged link <id>") because a judged warrant
    replaces a carried one in one act. The retirement is written first and its reason completed once
    the new link has an id: the partial unique index admits one live link per (figure, code)."""
    given = {col: code for col, code in (("identity_code", identity), ("icf_code", icf),
                                         ("needs_code", needs))
             if code is not None}
    if len(given) != 1:
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: name exactly one code, with one of --identity / --icf / --needs "
                      f"(got {len(given)}). Repeat the verb for each code. Nothing was written.")
    ((col, code),) = given.items()
    if not isinstance(code, str):
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: {col} must be one code as text, got {code!r}. Nothing was written.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        fig = conn.execute(
            "SELECT ref_id, claim_text, source_section "
            "FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
        if fig is None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id}: no such figure. Nothing was written.")
        _require_lens_code(conn, col, code)
        text = _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, fig["ref_id"], fig["claim_text"],
                                     fig["source_section"], "add-lens-link")
        held = conn.execute(
            f"SELECT link_id, basis FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=? AND {col}=? "
            f"AND retired_at IS NULL", (extraction_id, code)).fetchone()
        if held is not None and held["basis"] != "carried":
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id} already holds a live {held['basis']} link "
                f"({held['link_id']}) for {col} {code!r}. A figure holds one live link per code; retire it "
                f"first (retire-lens-link) if its warrant is wrong. Nothing was written.")
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
                "updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE link_id=?",
                [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), "superseded by judged link", dbcore.now(),
                 dbcore.session_stem(session), held["link_id"]])
        link_id = _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id, col, code, basis, text, session)
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute("UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retirement_reason=? WHERE link_id=?",
                         (f"superseded by judged link {link_id}", held["link_id"]))
        return {"link_id": link_id, "extraction_id": extraction_id, "lens": col, "code": code,
                "basis": basis, "retired_carried_link_id": held["link_id"] if held else None,
                "dry_run": dry_run}


def retire_lens_link(link_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire one lens link in place (OD-29): the three retired_* columns and the updated_* pair.

    Refuses: no such link; already retired; a blank reason; and the figure's LAST live link, because a
    figure with no lens is a value about nobody (D-0182) and the schema no longer holds that rule."""
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        link = conn.execute("SELECT extraction_id, retired_at FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE link_id=?",
                            (link_id,)).fetchone()
        if link is None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id}: no such link. Nothing was written.")
        if link["retired_at"] is not None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id} was retired at {link['retired_at']}. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        if not (reason or "").strip():
            raise Refusal("retire-lens-link: --reason is blank. Say why the figure is no longer stated "
                          "in this group. Nothing was written.")
        if conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_live_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=?",
                        (link["extraction_id"],)).fetchone()[0] == 1:
            raise Refusal(
                f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id} is extraction {link['extraction_id']}'s last live link. "
                f"Add the replacing link first with add-lens-link; a figure with no lens is a value about "
                f"nobody (D-0182). Nothing was written.")
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
            "updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE link_id=?",
            [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), reason.strip(), dbcore.now(),
             dbcore.session_stem(session), link_id])
        return {"link_id": link_id, "extraction_id": link["extraction_id"], "retired": True,
                "dry_run": dry_run}

if it appears in any source no matter the slug" and "add and expand parameter catalogue as
required" (catalogue-plan-v2, scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-
pilot/). What reaches the guidebook without these cases, by section:

  O  an observation that folds a second sense of a phrase into the first, or whose quote
     is not in the source it is attributed to -- vocabulary minted from words the source
     never used (critique F3, F7);
  S  a reading recorded as `full` over four pages of seventy-nine, or against bytes the
     source does not hold, or with a typed catalogue version -- so the catalogue implies
     "no code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code (F13);
  H  a full text that is not the whole document, or is not registered under the source;
  L  a parameter that cannot be retired, merged, renamed or un-declined, so every early
     mistake in a growing catalogue is permanent (F5) -- and, when it can, a merge that
     leaves rows pointing at the folded number;
  M  a name minted from an old item, or without the owner's recorded approval (D3);
  U  a cross-slug figure with no follow-up tag, or a live value resting on one silently (D1);
  E  a skimmed figure setting a published value (D1: "skimmed values are not publishable");
  A  the advisory backstops (observation quotes, scan debt, follow-ups, catalogue origins)
     unable to go red;

     the batch gate (R16-scan, R17);
  C  rows these writers produce that the capture path cannot ship.

pointed at a temp log holding fixture artefacts, so nothing touches retrieval-log/ or
data/. Fixtures are made through the writers. States no writer can make (a live
determination, a pre-rule admission) are set by SQL on the copy, each saying why. Every

import json

import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3

LOG = os.path.join(TMP, "retrieval-log")
shutil.copy(REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db", DB)
os.makedirs(LOG)
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"] = DB              # before db/dbcore resolve a path
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = LOG       # before retrieval_log reads LOG_ROOT

sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts" / "research"))

FIX = "session_fixture-scan-contract"

def record(tid, name, passed, details=""):
    results.append(bool(passed))
    print(f"  [{'✓' if passed else '✗'}] {tid}: {name}")
    if details and not passed:
        print(f"      {str(details)[:600]}")


def fn(name):
    """The db.py function, or a stub that raises -- so a missing verb is a red case."""
    f = getattr(db, name, None)
    if f is None:
        def missing(*a, **k):
            raise AttributeError(f"db.{name} does not exist")
        return missing
    return f


def refusal(f, *a, **k):
    """The Refusal's text if `f` refuses, else None (any other exception is a defect)."""
    try:
        f(*a, **k)
    except Refusal as exc:
        return str(exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- reported, never counted as a refusal
        print(f"      DEFECT, not a refusal: {exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}")
    return None


def expect_refusal(tid, name, needles, f, *a, **k):
    """record(): `f(*a, **k)` refuses, and the Refusal's text holds every needle."""
    msg = refusal(f, *a, **k)
    record(tid, name, msg and all(n in msg for n in
                                  ((needles,) if isinstance(needles, str) else needles)),
           msg)


def attempt(f, *a, **k):
    try:
        return f(*a, **k)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded red by the caller
        return {"error": f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}"}


def _absent_schema(exc):
    """A table or column T1 adds, missing because this is code (and a database) without
    T1. Reported and survived, so every later case still runs and goes red on its own --
    one missing table must not hide forty refusals."""
    return isinstance(exc, sqlite3.OperationalError) and (
        "no such table" in str(exc) or "no such column" in str(exc)
        or "has no column" in str(exc))

-- SCHEMA migration -- typed pointers from one term to another, each with its warrant (T-029, IMP-29; amended
-- 2026-11-17 by the propagation and consolidation adjudication, gaps G1 and G2; OD-56 answered by the owner 2026-11-14,
-- "b"; OD-29 resolved under delegation, "both retire in place"). Tooling, no research rows. Without it a ramp's
-- gradient and run length, or "this concept is broader than that one", are held as shared alias strings and prose, so
-- parameters that belong together cannot be shown together and an element page has nothing to derive from.
--
-- No AFTER_DATA marker: the table is new, so no committed data migration can INSERT into it.
--
-- THE THREE PLACES THAT RECORD A LIKENESS, one sentence each (a fact lives in one of them, rule 5):
--  * term_aliases relates a PHRASE to a term, by its alias_type (the values are that column's own CHECK:
--    dbcore.check_values(conn, 'term_aliases', 'alias_type')).
--  * term_relations (this table) relates a TERM to another term, by its kind (the values are `kind`'s own CHECK:
--    dbcore.check_values(conn, 'term_relations', 'kind')).
--  * T-032's relation rows relate a PROVISION to a provision at synthesis, judged at the Opus floor (OD-25 names their
--    kinds).
--
-- THE KINDS. A row reads "<from term> <kind> <to term>".
--  broader                 from is the broader concept and to the narrower one (a concept and what it includes).
--  part of                 from is a part of to.
--  element has parameter   from is a building element and to is a term one of its dimensions or quantities is
--                          measured by; to is normally the term of a parameter (base_parameters.term_id), which
--                          the reader looks up, not copies.
--  element has provision   from is a building element and to is a provision whose question is whether it is present
--                          (a hearing loop, a visual alarm, a tactile walking surface indicator); such a provision is
--                          not a parameter and no value is computed for it (OD-56). The row is the one home of "element
--                          E should carry provision P, per source S": the element-level determination (T-060) points
--                          at it and holds neither the provision term nor the warrant again.
--  adjacent                the two terms name things that meet or sit next to each other.
--  distinct                two terms a judge recorded as two concepts although their names are near or shared (a
--                          homonym, or a near name for another thing); written by add-term --distinct-from (T-129)
--                          and the consolidation pass (T-131), and read by T-130's proposer so that a judged pair is
--                          not proposed again until the base grows under it. Stored with the lower term id first.
-- `equivalent` is NOT a kind: two terms that name one concept are a dual home, and the act is a merge (T-129's
-- merge-term), never a standing pointer; until it merges them they are left as they are and listed. No reader needs a
-- "counterpart, not identical" kind, so none was added.
--
-- ONE LIVE ROW PER UNORDERED PAIR PER KIND. The unique index below is on the pair's lower and higher term id, so it
-- also refuses the converse of a directed row ("A broader B" while "B broader A" is live): a judge changes a relation
-- by retiring it with a reason and writing the new one, never by an UPDATE (OD-29, retire in place).
--
-- THE WARRANT is exactly one pointer, to the row that says it: an observation (observed_terms), an extraction
-- (source_value_extractions) or an adjudication (term_adjudications; the warrant of a `distinct` row written with its
-- term). `reason` is the judge's reason in words. Who judged it and when are created_by_session and created_at.
--
-- WRITERS: db.py add-term-relation, retire-term-relation. READERS: db.py element-parameters (an element's parameters
-- and provisions; T-033 and render read it); every later reader keeps `retired_at IS NULL`.

CREATE TABLE term_relations (
    relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    kind                TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (kind IN ('broader', 'part of', 'element has parameter', 'element has provision',
                                        'adjacent', 'distinct')),
    to_term_id          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    reason              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(reason)) > 0),
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    extraction_id       INTEGER REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    adjudication_id     INTEGER REFERENCES term_adjudications(adjudication_id),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    CHECK (from_term_id <> to_term_id),
    CHECK ((observation_id IS NOT NULL) + (extraction_id IS NOT NULL) + (adjudication_id IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct' OR from_term_id < to_term_id),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retirement_reason IS NULL)
        OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_relations_live_pair
    ON term_relations (kind, min(from_term_id, to_term_id), max(from_term_id, to_term_id))
 WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_term_relations_from ON term_relations (from_term_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_term_relations_to ON term_relations (to_term_id);

RETURNS None RATHER THAN RAISING when the schema cannot be read -- a missing or
    unreadable database must not make `db.py --help` fail, and the vocabulary is not lost
    by returning None: `check_declared()` refuses the same values at write time, with a

    """
    # ONE CONNECTION PER PROCESS, NOT ONE PER CALL, and the measurement is why. This
    # opened, queried and closed its own read-only connection every time. A fresh SQLite
    # connection's first query forces a parse of the whole schema -- 77 tables and 20
    # views -- so the call costs 2.28 ms where connect+close alone is 0.03 ms.
    #
    # db.py builds its argparse tree at import, and that tree contains 23 schema_choices
    # calls, so EVERY db.py invocation paid 62.6 ms before doing anything -- about 35% of
    # `db.py --help` (0.178 s wall), including subcommands that never touch the column in
    # question. The research sessions in this repo run db.py 60-136 times each, so it was
    # 3.4-7.7 seconds per session of pure startup. Through one shared connection the same
    # 23 calls cost 6.8 ms; cached, 4.6 ms.
    #

and false over an empty requirement (open owner question 5 of the 2026-11-06 round-3 adjudication,
`workplan/2026-11-06-run-pipeline-round-3-adjudication.md`). For a slug whose slug_status is neither `ACTIVE` nor
`STUB` it also reports owes_searches false: the slug named in merged_into owes them, so search there. **Current
editions only.** T4–T6 values are accepted as baselines; do not trace their history.

## 1. base — read before touching a source
The catalogue every source is read against: `base_parameters` + `terms`/`term_aliases`, the lenses
(`base_taxonomy_identity`, `access_needs`, `base_icf`),
`slugs`, `lang_jur_map`. Codes AND names; no bare axis codes or population umbrellas.
- **Equivalence before minting.** Search terms and aliases first. A phrase a source uses for a term we hold is an
  alias, reached only through the chain `observe-term` (its `--context-quote` must be found byte-for-byte in a file
  saved for the source: a `scripts/research/full_text.py` derivation or the fetched page) → `adjudicate-term
  --outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id` → `add-alias --alias-type` (from the CHECK; it writes `attestation`, `other_source`
  unless `--attestation instrument`). A form read where no observation exists takes the base route (`add-alias --alias
  --language --jurisdiction --source-url --source-page|--source-clause --attestation`; the pair must be in `lang_jur_map`);
  a search aid with no locator takes `--seed owner_supplied --approval-ref '<ledger heading naming it>'` and is never vocabulary (`--seed model_seed` is refused, OR-17).
  A row of `term_aliases` is one OCCURRENCE (T-028): the same form in another source, jurisdiction or locator is a new
  row with its own `form_id`; the usage of a form goes in `--usage-type` (DOMAIN, like TRANSLATION and DEPRECATED, is a
  legacy value no route writes). A search names the forms of its own language it fired with `log-search --form-id
  <form_id>`, never the label. `terms.canonical_en` is our English descriptive label, never a form; the name a page shows
  is derived by `v_term_names` (E1). A comparator ("not steeper than")
  or a value is not a name for the concept: adjudicate it `NOT-OURS`. The name rule is the writer's own: `add-term
  --canonical-en` and `rename-term --canonical-en` refuse a name carrying a digit, a comparison symbol, a `min` or
  `max` word, or a comparator word (`than`, `at least`, `at most`, `no more`, `no less`, `no fewer`, `no greater`,
  `not exceeding`, `exceed`); a definition is checked for digits, symbols and `min`/`max` only, because a definition is
  ordinary English. A duplicate parameter → `merge-parameter`; otherwise a new concept.
- **A new concept arises while a source is in hand** (`observe-term` needs `--ref-id` and a persisted quote), so base
  is re-entered from stages 3–4. **Claude never generates a phrase, name or alias** (OR-17): it is the source's own
  wording, present in its jurisdiction and language. `add-term --from-observation` mints the term and its NAMES-NEW
  adjudication together, and writes the observed phrase as the concept's first form (`unrecorded` until its quote is
  verified, then promoted by `add-alias`); the English label must sit inside the phrase only when the phrase is English.
  A concept met in a located form with no observation is minted by `add-term --first-form` with its language,
  jurisdiction, locator and `--attestation`, an English descriptive `--canonical-en`, and `--judge`. Both refuse a phrase whose observation is judged to name no term, a label
  another term holds, a form another term holds attested in the same language, and a near match (shared tokens with an
  attested form of the same language, or with a label when the name is English; a seed never counts, E4; a word in
  another language is another name, OD-68) unless `--distinct-from TERM-ID` names it and the rationale says why.
  `rename-term` takes one warrant (`--from-form <form_id>`, an attested English member form of the term; `--from-observation`; or `--ruling-quote`) and `--judge`, and
  records the former label in `term_label_picks`. `adjudicate-term` never writes NAMES-NEW. Owner approval is the data
  PR the owner reads (OR-17: "bulk, with me reading the PR"); `add-parameter` and `decline-parameter` take no
  approval flag; `--approval-ref` is the flag of the verbs that record an approval (derive them: `grep -n -F -- '"--approval-ref"' scripts/db.py`). `add-parameter` takes instead `--quantity-kind` and `--quantity-kind-observation-id` (T-020): the kind of quantity, from `base_quantity_kinds`, and the observation whose quote states a value of it.

  it (a relation is retired, never UPDATEd); `element-parameters --element` reads an element's parameters and
  provisions. There is no `equivalent` kind: two terms that name one concept are merged (T-129), not pointed at, and
  until `merge-term` exists they are left as they are and listed. A provision whose question is whether it is present
  (a hearing loop, a visual alarm) is related to its element by `element has provision` and is never made a parameter

CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
--   kind                subject
--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none. For a reading
-- they are the EFFECTIVE pair (see below), which is the pair the ledger owes.
-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. An older search row carries only a date; every other
-- row, and any search logged now, a minute.
--
-- WHAT STANDS, per kind (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
--   search        EVERY deferred search. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so a
--                 deferred search whose cell a later search covered still lists. Not derivable today.
--   mining        every citation_mining row whose OWN deferred_reason is set. The source's citation_mining_status is
--                 not read: it is one flag for every slug and both directions, so a pass for another slug sets it to
--                 'mined' while this row's deferral stands. `db.py log-mining --discharge-deferral` clears the row's
--                 deferred_reason, which is what ends it. A ref that resolves to no evidence_sources row (a lead
--                 anchor) is listed like any other. created_at is the ROW's.
--   reading       a deferral whose EFFECTIVE pair is still owed (v_reading_owed, the one definition). The effective
--                 source is the deferral's own, or its successor when the source is superseded (one hop); the
--                 effective parameter is the deferral's own, or the one it was merged into (one hop). A pair deferral
--                 stands iff its effective pair is owed; a whole-source deferral (NULL parameter) stands iff SOME
--                 active parameter of the effective source is owed. A retired parameter or a superseded successor
--                 leaves no ledger row, so it drops out. No date is read: a deferral can only be created while its
--                 cell is owed, and it stands for exactly as long as the cell is.
--   adjudication  an observation whose LATEST adjudication (highest adjudication_id, the rule alias and rename writers
--                 use) is DEFERRED: a later judgment of any other outcome discharges it.
SELECT 'search' AS kind,

Given in the session `session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMfdrQNV9XzGP4dyZm), in four typed messages while the second tooling stack was being built, the first after the coordinator reported that `term_label_picks.observation_id` and the warrant keys of `term_relations` point from base tables into the evidence stage, the third after the coordinator put the two questions of the term-name view (the sweep list of `session_2026-11-18-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack-2`) to the owner, and the fourth in answer to the coordinator's one question whether a base row may keep a source's `ref_id`. Server-clock times were not captured; derive them from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "absorbed by base and grounded" -- transcripts`).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "then the base grounds itself except for when evidence that allows for new terms/aliases/parameters to be found is pointed to as justification"
>
> "but this justification should then be absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there to prevent loops/recursion/sequencing conflicts"
>
> "likely have to do a convergence test for number of term appearances for concept or I rule"
>
> "ref_id as provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. A base row (a term, a form of it, a parameter, a relation, a label pick) may cite the evidence row (an observation, a source, an extraction) that allowed the item to be found, as its justification; that is the exception to "the base grounds itself" (2026-11-06, seventh statement) — basis: the first sentence].
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. "absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there" means the base keeps the justification in its OWN columns (what was found and where: the form, its language and jurisdiction, the source's URL, page and line, and the quoted words), so the base row reads, checks and orders without any evidence row, and nothing in the base waits on that evidence being admitted, adjudicated or verified, or is sequenced after it; the evidence stage keeps its own judgment, tier and verification of the source, which the base does not hold — basis: the second sentence and its stated purpose, "to prevent loops/recursion/sequencing conflicts"; this keeps CLAUDE.md rule 5 (a fact in one home) where it can: where a form was found is the base's fact, the source's standing is the evidence stage's].
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-71. A base row may keep the source's `ref_id` (or an observation id) beside the absorbed grounding, and that is ONLY provenance: nothing in the base validates against it, orders after it, joins through it to decide a state, or waits on it; a base writer neither requires it nor refuses a row for lacking it — basis: "ref_id as provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"]. The wording of the owner's second statement on whether the quoted words are repeated in the base row (or only the locator) is NOT stated and is not read in.
- [ASSUMPTION: OD-72. "number of term appearances for concept" means the number of occurrences of a form among a concept's forms (the rows of `term_aliases`, one per occurrence since migration 146), and "a convergence test" means the displayed name is the form whose appearances converge, and "or I rule" means the owner may set the name by a named judge's pick as OD-38 already provides — basis: the words; "likely" marks a direction, not a settled rule].

OD-71: the base grounds itself; evidence that allowed a new term, form or parameter is absorbed into the base's own columns
OD-71 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

OD-72: displayed name by a convergence test on the appearances of a form for a concept, or the owner's ruling; the test is not specified
OD-72 STATUS: REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER

**What it does.**

- **OD-71.** A base table holds no foreign key into the evidence stage and no pointer that a base row's validity waits on. Where a base row is justified by evidence, the justification is written into the base row's own cells. Sequencing runs one way only: evidence may be found and named from the base; the base is never ordered after evidence. It reaches `term_label_picks.observation_id` and `add-term --from-observation`'s hold of a form `unrecorded` until a quote verifies (T-028), the warrant keys of `term_relations` (T-029), `term_aliases`' own source columns, and any later base table that carries a warrant.

    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),

    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((form_id IS NOT NULL) + (ruling_quote IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (former_label IS NOT NULL OR form_id IS NOT NULL)
);

-- 151_term_relations_ground_in_base.sql
-- SCHEMA migration, compensating 147 and 148 (T-029 repair; owner statements 2026-11-18, OD-71: "the base grounds itself
-- except for when evidence that allows for new terms/aliases/parameters to be found is pointed to as justification; but
-- this justification should then be absorbed by base and grounded as if it were always there", and "ref_id as
-- provenance? sure. but it's ONLY for provenance"). No data rows.
--
-- term_relations (a base table) carried three foreign keys out of the base: observation_id to observed_terms (evidence),
-- extraction_id to source_value_extractions and adjudication_id to term_adjudications (judgment). It is rebuilt without
-- them. A relation's justification is now the base's own cells:
--  * WHERE IT WAS FOUND: source_url, source_page, source_line and source_clause, spelled and checked as term_aliases
--    spells them (one fact, one spelling). A locator is a URL plus a page or a clause; a locator part without the URL
--    says nowhere. Only the locator is absorbed, not the source's quoted words (the ruling does not say they are).
--  * WHY: `reason`, the judge's reason in words. A `distinct` relation is a judgment between two concepts the base
--    already holds, so it rests on its reason alone (its rationale, absorbed: the base does not wait on, or point into,
--    the judgment stage); every other kind rests on the located statement that says so. An `element has provision` row
--    is therefore never justified by a reason alone (OD-56: it rests on the source statement that says the element
--    should carry the provision).
--  * ref_id is PROVENANCE ONLY: nullable, no foreign key, validated against nothing, read by no base decision.
-- Rows are copied as they stand; a row without a locator that is not `distinct` cannot be copied and the CHECK aborts the
-- migration rather than drop it (none existed when this was written: `select count(*) from term_relations`).
-- Everything else is 147's and 148's, unchanged: the kinds, the retirement cells, the order of a `distinct` row, and
-- the one live row per unordered pair per kind.

CREATE TABLE _151_term_relations (
    relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    kind                TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (kind IN ('broader', 'part of', 'element has parameter', 'element has provision',
                                        'adjacent', 'distinct')),
    to_term_id          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    reason              TEXT CHECK (reason IS NULL OR length(trim(reason)) > 0),
    source_url          TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'
         OR source_url GLOB 'https://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')
        AND source_url NOT GLOB '*[' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')),
    source_page         TEXT
    CHECK (source_page IS NULL OR TRIM(source_page, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    source_line         INTEGER
    CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR (typeof(source_line) = 'integer' AND source_line > 0)),
    source_clause       TEXT
    CHECK (source_clause IS NULL OR TRIM(source_clause, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    ref_id              TEXT,                                               -- provenance only (OD-71): no foreign key
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    CHECK (from_term_id <> to_term_id),
    CHECK (source_url IS NOT NULL
           OR (source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL AND source_clause IS NULL)),
    CHECK (kind = 'distinct' OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL))),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct' OR reason IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct'
           OR CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
              < CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
           OR (CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               = CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               AND from_term_id < to_term_id)),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL)),
    CHECK (retired_at IS NULL OR (length(trim(retired_at)) > 0 AND length(trim(retired_by_session)) > 0
                                  AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
);

INSERT INTO _151_term_relations (relation_id, from_term_id, kind, to_term_id, reason, source_url, source_page,
                                 source_line, source_clause, ref_id, created_at, created_by_session, retired_at,
                                 retired_by_session, retirement_reason)
SELECT relation_id, from_term_id, kind, to_term_id, reason, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, created_at,
       created_by_session, retired_at, retired_by_session, retirement_reason
  FROM term_relations;

DROP TABLE term_relations;
ALTER TABLE _151_term_relations RENAME TO term_relations;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_relations_live_pair
    ON term_relations (kind, min(from_term_id, to_term_id), max(from_term_id, to_term_id))
 WHERE retired_at IS NULL;

PRAGMA user_version = 151;
PY

def add_term_relation(from_term: str, kind: str, to_term: str, reason, session: str, *,
                      observation_id: int = None, extraction_id: int = None, adjudication_id: int = None,
                      dry_run: bool = False):
    """Write one `term_relations` row: '<from term> <kind> <to term>', with the row that says so (T-029).

    The kinds are the column's own CHECK (`dbcore.check_declared`); the migration's DDL comment says what each means
    and which way it reads. There is no `equivalent` kind: two terms that name one concept are merged (T-129), never
    pointed at. Refuses, each sentence naming the next act: a kind the CHECK does not hold; a blank reason; an
    unknown term; the same term twice; no warrant, or more than one; a warrant row that does not exist; and a second
    live row of the same kind for the same pair in either direction (retire the held one first, with its reason). A

               a1.get("relation_id") and [p["term_id"] for p in r1.get("provisions", [])] == [P29]
               and r1.get("parameters") == []

                    pv1.get("source_clause")) == (URL29, "3", 12, None)

               and pv1.get("created_by_session") == T29S, (a1, r1))

               e2 and all(k in e2 for k in KINDS29) and "equivalent" not in KINDS29 and "distinct" in KINDS29
               and len(rels()) == n02, (e2, KINDS29))

        # T029-03: `element has parameter` reads the parameter of the term it points at by looking it up.
        a3 = attempt(addrel, E29, K_PAR, PT29, "TASK-FIXTURE: the element's dimension", T29S, **LOC29B)
        r3 = attempt(elemread, E29)

               "term carries (looked up, not copied) and its clause locator; a provision that carries no "
               "parameter prints none",
               a3.get("relation_id") and len(pr3) == 1 and pr3[0]["term_id"] == PT29
               and pr3[0]["parameter_id"] == PID29 and pr3[0]["source_clause"] == "TASK-FIXTURE 4.1"
               and [p["parameter_id"] for p in r3["provisions"]] == [None], (a3, r3))

        # T029-04 (amendment 1): `distinct` is stored with the lower term id first whichever way the pair is named,
        # rests on its reason alone, and a second live row for the pair is refused naming the held row.
        lo, hi = sorted((P29, O29))

               "it is named; a second live row of the pair, either way round, is refused naming the held relation "

               a4.get("relation_id") and (a4.get("from_term_id"), a4.get("to_term_id")) == (lo, hi)

               and all(e and str(a4["relation_id"]) in e and "retire-term-relation" in e for e in (e4a, e4b)),

        # T029-05 (rule 5): the converse of a directed row is a second home of one fact, refused by the same
        # index; a different kind between the same pair is not.
        a5 = attempt(addrel, E29, "broader", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE: broader", T29S, **LOC29)
        e5 = refusal(addrel, O29, "broader", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE: converse", T29S, **LOC29)
        a5b = attempt(addrel, O29, "part of", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE: another kind", T29S, **LOC29)

               and a5b.get("relation_id"), (a5, e5, a5b))

        # T029-06 (OD-71): the justification is the base's own cells. Each of these is refused, naming what is
        # required, and writes nothing: no locator on a kind but `distinct` (a reason alone does not justify it),
        # a URL with no page or clause, a page with no URL, a URL that is not http(s), a line below 1, a blank
        # page, and a `distinct` row with no reason.
        n06 = len(rels())
        e6 = {"none": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE: reason only", T29S),
              "url only": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, source_url=URL29),
              "page only": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, source_page="3"),
              "scheme": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, source_url="ftp://x.org/a",
                                source_page="3"),
              "line": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, source_line=0, **LOC29B),
              "blank page": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, source_url=URL29,
                                    source_page="  ", source_clause="c"),
              "distinct no reason": refusal(addrel, E29, "distinct", O29, None, T29S, **LOC29),
              "distinct partial locator": refusal(addrel, E29, "distinct", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S,
                                                  source_url=URL29)}
        record("T029-06", "no locator, a partial or malformed one, and a `distinct` row with no reason are each "
               "refused, naming what is required, and write nothing",
               all(e6.values()) and "--source-url" in e6["none"] and "--source-page or --source-clause" in e6["none"]
               and "--reason" in e6["distinct no reason"] and len(rels()) == n06, e6)

        # T029-07: a blank reason, an unknown term and one term at both ends are each refused.
        e7 = {"reason": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", O29, "   ", T29S, **LOC29),
              "term": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", "TASK-FIXTURE-NO-SUCH-TERM", "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, **LOC29),
              "self": refusal(addrel, E29, "adjacent", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE", T29S, **LOC29)}
        record("T029-07", "a blank reason, an unknown term and the same term at both ends are each refused and "
               "write nothing", e7["reason"] and "--reason" in e7["reason"] and e7["term"] and "no such term" in
               e7["term"] and e7["self"] and "both ends" in e7["self"] and "two different terms" in e7["self"]
               and len(rels()) == n06, e7)

        # T029-08 (amendment 2): a relation is retired in place with a reason, never revived, and the reader keeps
        # only live rows; the pair can then be written again.
        id8 = a1["relation_id"]
        z8 = refusal(retrel, id8, "  ", T29S)
        d8 = attempt(retrel, id8, "TASK-FIXTURE: the source was withdrawn", T29S)

        row8 = q("SELECT retired_at, retired_by_session, retirement_reason, reason, kind, source_url FROM "
                 "term_relations WHERE relation_id=?", id8)
        r8 = attempt(elemread, E29)
        w8 = attempt(addrel, E29, K_PROV, P29, "TASK-FIXTURE: written again", T29S, **LOC29)
        record("T029-08", "retire-term-relation retires in place with a reason (the row stays, its other cells "
               "untouched), refuses a blank reason, a retired row and an unknown one; the reader drops it; the "
               "pair can be written again", z8 and d8.get("retired") is True and again8 and "retired at" in again8
               and nosuch8 and "no such relation" in nosuch8 and "select relation_id" in nosuch8
               and row8 and row8[0][0] and row8[0][1] == dbcore.session_stem(T29S)
               and row8[0][2] == "TASK-FIXTURE: the source was withdrawn"
               and row8[0][3] == "TASK-FIXTURE: the element should carry the provision" and row8[0][4] == K_PROV
               and row8[0][5] == URL29
               and r8.get("provisions") == [] and w8.get("relation_id") and w8["relation_id"] != id8,
               (z8, d8, again8, nosuch8, row8, r8, w8))

        # T029-09: the schema holds what the writers hold, so a route past the writers meets the same refusals.
        def raw(sql, *a):
            c = sqlite3.connect(DB)
            try:
                c.execute(sql, a)
                c.commit()
                return None
            except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                return str(exc)
            finally:
                c.close()
        ins = ("INSERT INTO term_relations (from_term_id, kind, to_term_id, reason, source_url, source_page, "
               "created_at, created_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 't', 't')")
        lo9, hi9 = sorted((E29, O29))        # a pair with no live `distinct` row, so only the CHECK can refuse
        raw9 = {
            "a": ("no locator on a kind but `distinct`", raw(ins, E29, "adjacent", P29, "TASK-FIXTURE", None, None)),
            "b": ("a `distinct` row stored higher id first", raw(ins, hi9, "distinct", lo9, "TASK-FIXTURE", None,
                                                                 None)),
            "c": ("one term at both ends", raw(ins, E29, "adjacent", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE", URL29, "3")),
            "e": ("a kind outside the CHECK", raw(ins, E29, "equivalent", O29, "TASK-FIXTURE", URL29, "3")),
            "f": ("the converse of a live row of the same kind", raw(ins, O29, "broader", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE",
                                                                    URL29, "3")),
            "g": ("a `distinct` row with no reason", raw(ins, lo9, "distinct", hi9, None, None, None)),
            "h": ("a page with no URL", raw(ins, lo9, "distinct", hi9, "TASK-FIXTURE", None, "3")),
            "i": ("a URL that is not http(s)", raw(ins, E29, "adjacent", P29, "TASK-FIXTURE", "ftp://x.org/a", "3")),
        }

        bad9d = []
        for mask in range(1, 7):          # every proper, non-empty subset of the three cells set

        if not raw("UPDATE term_relations SET " + ", ".join(f"{c}=?" for c in RET) + " WHERE relation_id=?",

        for i, c in enumerate(RET):       # all three set, exactly one of them blank

        record("T029-09d", "the schema refuses a retirement with any one or two of its three cells set, any all-"
               "three set with one or all of them blank (a NULL reason passes a length check, so the form is the "
               "siblings' equality)", not bad9d and q("SELECT retired_at FROM term_relations WHERE relation_id=?",
                                                       w8["relation_id"]) == [(None,)], bad9d)
        for key, (what, err) in raw9.items():

                   bool(err), err)

        # T029-10: the table is in the derived capture set, so a relation made on a scratch copy reaches the
        # canonical database through emit_batch_sql.
        con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
        try:
            cap29 = set(dbcore.writable_tables(con))
        finally:
            con.close()
        record("T029-10", "term_relations is in the derived capture set (dbcore.writable_tables)",
               "term_relations" in cap29)

        # T029-11: the reader refuses an unknown element, in a sentence; through the CLI it exits 1, not a traceback.
        r11 = run("element-parameters", "--element", "TASK-FIXTURE-NO-SUCH-TERM")
        record("T029-11", "element-parameters refuses an unknown element in a sentence",
               r11.returncode == 1 and r11.stderr.startswith("REFUSING:") and "no such term" in r11.stderr
               and "Traceback" not in r11.stderr, (r11.returncode, r11.stderr[-200:]))

        # T029-12: the CLI is wired for each verb, takes a kind containing spaces and the grounding flags; the
        # vocabulary offered is the CHECK's own.
        r12 = run("add-term-relation", "--from-term", O29, "--kind", "adjacent", "--to-term", P29, "--reason",
                  "TASK-FIXTURE: via the CLI", "--source-url", URL29, "--source-clause", "TASK-FIXTURE 9",

        id12 = json.loads(r12.stdout).get("relation_id") if r12.returncode == 0 and r12.stdout.strip() else None
        r12b = run("retire-term-relation", "--relation-id", str(id12), "--reason", "TASK-FIXTURE: via the CLI",

               "exactly the column's own CHECK set", id12 and r12b.returncode == 0
               and all(k in r12c.stdout.replace("\n", " ") for k in KINDS29)
               and q("SELECT retired_at IS NOT NULL FROM term_relations WHERE relation_id=?", id12) == [(1,)],
               (r12.returncode, r12.stderr[-200:], r12b.returncode, r12b.stderr[-200:]))

                      and n.func.value.id == "p_atr" and n.args and isinstance(n.args[0], ast.Constant)

               "\"kind\"), not a typed list", len(ch12) == 1 and isinstance(ch12[0], ast.Call)
               and getattr(ch12[0].func, "attr", None) == "schema_choices"
               and [a.value for a in ch12[0].args if isinstance(a, ast.Constant)] == ["term_relations", "kind"],
               [ast.dump(c) for c in ch12])

        # T029-13 (OD-56, OD-71): a provision is justified by where a source says the element should carry it,
        # never by a reason alone (the old rule, that an adjudication is no warrant, in the base's own terms): the
        # writer refuses it naming the locator, and the schema refuses it; with a locator it is accepted.

        e13 = refusal(addrel, O29, K_PROV, P29, "TASK-FIXTURE: a reason alone", T29S)
        r13 = raw(ins, O29, K_PROV, P29, "TASK-FIXTURE: a reason alone", None, None)
        a13 = attempt(addrel, O29, K_PROV, P29, None, T29S, **LOC29B)

        r14 = raw(ins, E29, "adjacent", P29, "  ", URL29, "3")

        # (no writer builds a merged or retired state without a figure to merge); ids are derived from the form of
        # the held ids.
        pre = q("SELECT substr(term_id, 1, instr(term_id, '-')) FROM terms ORDER BY term_id LIMIT 1")[0][0]

                                             ("lo", 9998), ("hi", 10001))}

            record("T029-15", "the fixture term ids are free", False, FT)
        else:

                x("INSERT INTO terms (term_id, canonical_en, created_at, created_by_session, updated_at, "

            for n in ("keep", "fold", "gone"):

            r15 = attempt(elemread, E29)

            e15r = refusal(addrel, E29, K_PAR, FT["gone"], None, T29S, **LOC29)

                   and by15[FT["fold"]]["parameter_term_id"] == FT["keep"]
                   and by15[FT["fold"]]["merged_from_parameter_id"] == pid["fold"], (w15, by15.get(FT["fold"])))

                   by15.get(FT["nope"], {}).get("parameter_id", 0) is None and by15[FT["nope"]]["declined"] is True
                   and by15[FT["fold"]]["declined"] is False, by15.get(FT["nope"]))
            record("T029-15c", "a new `element has parameter` row to a term whose parameter is merged names the "

                   e15m and FT["keep"] in e15m and e15r and "retired" in e15r and a15.get("relation_id"),

            record("T029-16", "a `distinct` row between a 4-digit and a 5-digit id is stored with the numerically "

                   (a16.get("from_term_id"), a16.get("to_term_id")) == (FT["lo"], FT["hi"]) and r16, (a16, r16))

        # stage (its only foreign keys are into terms); its ref_id is a plain provenance cell: any text is
        # accepted, validated against nothing, printed by the reader and read by no decision.

        fk29 = [(f[2], SM29.get(f[2])) for f in q("PRAGMA foreign_key_list(term_relations)")]

                      **LOC29)
        a17b = attempt(addrel, P29, "adjacent", E29, "TASK-FIXTURE: no provenance", T29S, **LOC29)
        record("T029-17", "term_relations, a base table, holds no foreign key into another stage; ref_id is a "
               "plain nullable cell, accepted unvalidated and equally absent",
               SM29.get("term_relations") == "base" and fk29 and all(st == "base" for _, st in fk29)
               and "ref_id" in cols29 and a17.get("relation_id") and a17b.get("relation_id")
               and q("SELECT ref_id FROM term_relations WHERE relation_id IN (?, ?) ORDER BY relation_id",
                     a17["relation_id"], a17b["relation_id"]) == [("TASK-FIXTURE-NOT-A-REF",), (None,)],

- **Three places record a likeness, and a fact lives in one of them.** `term_aliases` relates a **phrase** to a term, by
  its `alias_type` (the column's own CHECK holds the values). `term_relations` relates a **term to another term**, by its
  `kind` (the column's own CHECK holds the values; the migration's DDL comment defines each kind and which way it reads).
  T-032's relation rows relate a **provision to a provision** at synthesis, judged at the Opus floor (OD-25).
  `add-term-relation --from-term --kind --to-term` plus exactly one of `--observation-id`, `--extraction-id`
  or `--adjudication-id` (the row that says so; an `element has provision` row takes the first two only, OD-56) and an
  optional `--reason` writes one row; `retire-term-relation --relation-id --reason` changes
  it (a relation is retired, never UPDATEd); `element-parameters --element` reads an element's parameters (a merged one followed to the parameter that
